title: Sample B has a spherical subpopulation that fails 3.12 µm channels
summary: In this synthetic demo pair, 25% of cells in sample B have a sphericity index above 0.85, versus 0% in sample A. The simulated passage curves give D50 = 2.99 µm (A) and 3.16 µm (B). This is a hypothesis to test, not a diagnosis.

findings.text: 25% of cells in sample B have a sphericity index above 0.85, versus 0% in sample A.
Half of the cells pass without membrane strain at 2.99 µm in A and 3.16 µm in B.
At 3.12 µm the predicted pass fraction is 87% for A versus 43% for B.

consistency_flags.note: Approximation V∝D³; smear artefacts widen the image CV.

experiment.hypothesis: At 3.12 µm, synthetic_healthy passes at 87% vs synthetic_hs at 43%, driven by surface-to-volume ratio alone.
experiment.falsified_if: Measured pass fractions do not differ, or the difference disappears after osmotic swelling/shrinking controls.
caveats: Model assumes cylindrical channels; rectangular microfluidic channels need an equivalent-diameter correction.
Stiffness is not modelled; rigid cells may fail where geometry allows passage.

limitations: Sphericity is inferred from central pallor.
No mechanical simulation: the passage verdict is geometric only.
Synthetic demo populations, not patient data.
